headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, thereby protecting residential ratepayers from cost increases.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: U.S. Sen. Mark Warner, Dominion Energy, consumer advocacy and utility watchdog organizations, Governor Abigail Spanberger.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (initially concerned about language).
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, aiming to prevent residential customers from bearing the burden of grid upgrades. The bill seeks to ensure data centers cover their own infrastructure costs, which could otherwise increase residential bills by 1.5% to 5%.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to report their water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Potomac Conservancy, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental and water advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (expressed concerns about being singled out, but generally compliant).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption, especially in Northern Virginia.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to evaluate sound profiles and other environmental impacts on nearby residential areas and schools.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, Manassas City Council, Piedmont Environmental Council, Loudoun County Supervisor Mike Turner.
opponents: Data center developers (implied by stricter regulations and pushback against noise complaints).
news_headline: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules
news_summary: Manassas City Council unanimously approved stricter zoning rules for data centers, addressing noise, appearance, and proximity concerns near residential areas. This move reflects growing concerns in Northern Virginia localities about data center impacts, with some residents resorting to extreme measures to block noise.
